summary: Strong on rules and process (law, conflict review, scored priority list, AGREE II threshold, payer link); weak on single funding channel, nominator-driven scoring, local data.

evidence.text: Universal Health Care Act 2019, Section 27(c): the Department of Health sets clinical standards through guidelines, with societies and academe
Three orders in five years: 2018-0019, 2021-0020, 2023-0002
Disease Prevention and Control Bureau oversees; National Practice Guidelines Secretariat (agenda pp. 5, 24)
Programme started 2018 and was re-issued in 2023 and given a 2024 agenda after the 2022 change of government
15 organisations incl. PhilHealth, the Health Technology Assessment Council, municipal health officers and a patient group, but on the topic committee only (agenda p. 5)
Mandate in the flagship health law; Secretary's foreword to the agenda
Department of Health funds the top 50 topics, 10 a year (agenda p. 66)
Topics ranked 51-75 are endorsed to development partners and professional societies for funding (agenda p. 66)
All public funding goes through UP National Institutes of Health "until enabling mechanisms are in place" (agenda p. 81)
Five weighted criteria from a scoping review, scheduled annual review (agenda pp. 17-21, 66)
116 nominations from societies, pharmaceutical companies, hospitals and programmes (agenda p. 19)
Scored "primarily" from the nomination form; news articles and lecture videos accepted (agenda pp. 21-22)
15 organisations, 3 scorers per cluster, 75% consensus (agenda pp. 19, 22-23)
Burden weighted 30 of 100 points, but 113 of 116 nominations were adult (agenda pp. 19-20)
Top 50 scheduled for funding; local data gaps flagged for research (agenda pp. 65-66)
74 people in 45 institutions able to develop guidelines (Dans et al., 2021)
45 institutions capable, but one receives all public guideline funding
About half able to handle equity, one third with conflict-of-interest experience (Dans et al.)
Plan is 10 a year; members cite "lengthy timelines" (agenda p. 30)
2018 national manual; 2021 order covers development, adoption and dissemination
Missing local data named as the main bottleneck; national health data repository still being built (agenda p. 64)
Periodic health examination guidelines adapted with GRADE-ADOLOPMENT
National guidelines must reach 75% on AGREE II rigour and editorial independence
Old guidelines re-nominated for update (neonatal sepsis 2019, transfusion 2009) rather than on a set cycle (agenda pp. 31, 45)
Independent review committee; financial versus non-financial rules (agenda pp. 19-20)
Financial conflicts excluded at nomination; all non-financial "Allowed; Broadcast", incl. a society's Novartis partnership (agenda pp. 10-11)
Topic nominators may sit on the steering committee or consensus panel (agenda p. 81)
Committee conflicts published; public guideline platform
Public consultation, 53 stakeholders, 7 appeals, no changes (agenda pp. 23-24)
Breast cancer package protocols are "based on the Clinical Practice Guidelines"; contracted hospitals must adopt the pathway (PhilHealth Circular 2024-0007)
2026 osimertinib assessment calls for a guideline update; guideline drugs missing from the formulary, talks ongoing (agenda p. 64)
Quality-improvement order requires hospitals to monitor compliance with guidelines and pathways (Order 2020-0034)
21 contracted facilities for the breast cancer package
Not found; likely weak point under devolution
One adherence study (COVID-19, two tertiary hospitals)
Online guideline platform, Department Circulars, social media
Barrier study of the adaptation project
Agenda will track funded topics, money allocated, guidelines used in policy (agenda p. 66)
One adherence study
2017 situational analysis and 2021 capacity mapping predate the expanded programme
Agenda asks academe to align research; gaps listed (agenda pp. 16, 65)
